cohort: The study included 219,950 primiparous women aged 20-34 years with singleton, term pregnancies without malpresentations.
finding: Being overweight or obese was independently associated with an increased likelihood of cesarean births among low-risk primiparous women.
mod_finding: Being overweight or obese was independently associated with an increased likelihood of cesarean births, with overweight not being an independent risk factor for elective cesarean births.
